newsitem.title: USA: E*Trade aims to double accounts in FY97.
newsitem.headline: E*Trade aims to double accounts in FY97.

text.p: E*Trade Group Inc is looking to continue adding accounts at a pace to double its customer base a year from now, the company's top executive said.

"We're still adding about 300 accounts per day," E*Trade president and chief executive Christos Cotsakos said in an interview. "We have more people either converting their accounts or holding double accounts."

The strong account growth helped the Palo Alto, California-based online brokerage firm post a $0.02 per share fourth quarter profit, flat versus a year ago. According to First Call, analysts were expecting a break-even quarter.
Cost control and efficiency efforts, such as a decision to shift to self-clearing, helped fuel the fourth quarter profit and contributed to a sharp increase in E*Trade's asset base.
But account growth continues to be the primary driver for E*Trade, which completed an initial public offering in August.
E*Trade had 91,400 active accounts at September's end, the close of its fiscal year. That figure was up 24 percent from a quarter ago and 186 percent for the year.
Cotsakos said the company planned to grow its account base by about seven percent per month, with a target customer base of 200,000 by the end of fiscal 1997.

He declined to offer a profit outlook for the coming year, however, citing the uncertain outcome of next week's California vote on Proposition 211, an initiative intended to ease the filing of securities lawsuits.
